The area around the Vincent Thomas Bridge and Point Fermin Park is typical of where we work here.

Recent San Pedro requests cluster around two ideas: flame color and brightness control by remote or app for the main living wall in Point Fermin, and a calmer, quieter composition for a primary bedroom in Vista del Oro. The materials stay consistent - the proportions do the adapting.

A electric fireplace wall also solves practical problems: cables disappear, equipment gets ventilation and access, and the TV lands at the right height for your sofa - not wherever the studs happened to be.

How we build a electric fireplace wall

Electric units changed what a fireplace wall can be. No flue means the wall can go almost anywhere; no gas line means no utility permits; and modern linear flames look right in a contemporary room in a way a gas insert in a fake chimney never did.

Questions from San Pedro homeowners

How much does an electric fireplace wall cost in San Pedro?

Electric fireplace walls in San Pedro start at $5,900 including the framed wall build and finish; the fireplace unit itself is priced by size and brand in your estimate. Most complete projects fall between $6,500 and $11,000.

Is it safe to mount the TV above an electric fireplace?

Yes, with correct clearances. Electric units vent heat forward from the top of the unit, and we build the mantel depth and TV position to the manufacturer's spec - the TV stays within its safe temperature range.

Does an electric fireplace actually heat the room?

Most units include a 1,500W heater that warms roughly 400-500 sq ft as supplemental heat. Flame and heat run independently, so you can have the flame in summer with the heater off.

Do I need an electrician or a permit?

The fireplace plugs into or hardwires to a standard circuit; if a new outlet is needed inside the wall we coordinate it. Framing a non-structural accent wall with an electric unit generally does not need the permits a gas or wood fireplace would.
